> No error is thrown.

Almost no error...

> C:\AI\ComfyUI\comfy\utils.py:1024: RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in cast
>   images = [Image.fromarray(np.**clip**(255. * image.cpu().numpy(), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)) for image in samples]
> 
> C:\AI\ComfyUI\nodes.py:1662: RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in cast
> img = Image.fromarray(np.**clip**(i, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8))

Something with "clip"?

1. Try the simple clip loader "Load CLIP" instead of the gguf loader you use for your safetensors file, maybe what's working with turbo isn't with the base model.

2. Try one of the default qwen3 4b safentensors clips, to test if that's working ( https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/z_image/tree/main/split_files/text_encoders or smaller gguf versions of it). If that's okay, there is an incompatibility with the z-image base model and the specific variant of qwen3 4b you use.

But I've tested it and could use a variant of qwen3 4b, qwen3-4b-abliterated-v2-q8_0.gguf:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0da6a317-c5f6-4ad2-aa61-8731dcb72ae4)

I did some further testing by setting up a completely fresh ComfyUI installation on a different SSD to isolate the issue. Here are the results, which strongly point to Attention optimization conflicts. [Screenshot 1: Fresh ComfyUI Install (New SSD)] Result 1 (Left): Default settings (No SageAttention). -> Success! The image generated perfectly. Result 2 (Middle): Installed triton_windows-3.6.0 and ran with the SageAttention enabled. -> Failed (Black Image). Result 3 (Right): Triton is installed, but ran with default settings (SageAttention disabled). -> Success! [Screenshot 2: Old ComfyUI Install] Generated using the default SDPA option (SageAttention disabled). -> Failed (Black Image). Even without Sage, the old environment still outputs black images. This implies that leftover dependencies or hidden cross-attention settings in older/messier environments also trigger the NaN issue for the Base model. [Screenshot 3: Output Folder from Old ComfyUI] This shows my output folder from the old environment. The normal, successfully generated images are from the Z-Image Turbo model. The solid black images are from the Z-Image Base model, generated using the exact same workflow. Conclusion: The silent NaN / black image issue with the Z-Image Base model appears to be highly sensitive to Attention optimization methods (like SageAttention) and the underlying PyTorch environment (especially on AMD/ROCm). While the Turbo model survives these environments without issue, the Base model's tensors seem to collapse instantly when certain optimizations are applied or if the environment dependencies aren't perfectly clean.

@dkspwndj 
Your test matrix is really clear. The interesting gap is between Result 3 (fresh install, Triton installed, SageAttention off → works) and the old environment with the same config failing. That's probably cached Triton compilation artifacts. Triton caches compiled kernels, and those cached versions from when SageAttention was active can still get loaded even after you disable it in ComfyUI settings.
Z-Image Base seems more precision-sensitive than Turbo on AMD/ROCm. From what I've seen, some Triton kernel paths can produce slightly different numerical results on AMD vs CUDA, and Base apparently doesn't tolerate that while Turbo does. That would also explain why Forge Neo works fine, it likely dispatches attention through a different path.
To fix the old environment: pip uninstall triton triton-windows, clear the Triton compilation cache (usually under ~/.triton/ or the Windows equivalent), and restart. Otherwise your clean install without Triton is probably the most reliable.
